report:
## Conclusion

**The claim is accurate.** Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, 19.5 mg) is FDA-approved for the prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years.

This is confirmed by the official FDA-approved product labeling on DailyMed, which states under "Indications and Usage" that "Kyleena is a progestin-containing intrauterine system (IUS) indicated for prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years" (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080). The original FDA label filed with the agency similarly states, "Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years," based on a cumulative 5-year pregnancy rate derived from clinical trial data (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/208224s000lbl.pdf).

Bayer's own product monograph corroborates this, noting that "Following insertion into the uterine cavity, KYLEENA... is effective for up to 5 years. KYLEENA must be removed by the end of the fifth year and can be replaced at the time of removal with a new KYLEENA if continued contraceptive protection is desired" (https://www.bayer.com/sites/default/files/2020-11/kyleena-pm-en.pdf).

Additionally, Drugs.com's FDA approval history notes that Kyleena received FDA approval on September 16, 2016, specifically "for Prevention of Pregnancy for up to Five Years," with clinical trial data showing a Pearl-Index of 0.29 after five years, making it more than 99% effective per year of use (https://www.drugs.com/history/kyleena.html).

All sources consistently and unambiguously support the claim, with no conflicting information found.
